decisions.reason: Because this automation product builds directly on the firm's existing control, monitoring, and energy-efficiency know-how, its strong absorptive capacity makes further learning and improvement more likely than withdrawal.

The fouling detection system fits the firm's established installed-base monitoring and optimisation capabilities, so in-house R&D and research cooperation support continued refinement rather than exit.

Although newer and somewhat more adjacent than core software products, the spring-controlled flap weir is still close enough to the firm's hydraulic infrastructure knowledge base that management would normally keep it and learn from field use.
An energy management system for water facilities is highly aligned with the firm's strategic move toward digitally networked, efficient, energy-aware infrastructure, making retention very likely.

The overflow flap gate product line is close to the firm's established water-level regulation business and benefits from accumulated project know-how across several models, so commercial application and incremental improvement are more plausible than withdrawal.
